Applied AI / Infrastructure

Making engineering

I built ReAct agents that turn Slack and GitHub context into runbooks for engineers. Behind the agent, I developed a Python MCP server, deployed Milvus on OpenShift, and automated ingestion with Jenkins.

The work went beyond retrieval: evaluating failures, reviewing changes, and communicating clearly made the system more reliable.

AI agents / Full-stack

Better tools for
the on-call engineer.

I shipped a LangGraph agent for payroll incident triage, connecting investigation tools with a React dashboard for traces, output review, and approvals.

Building the workflow end to end taught me to make an agent’s work understandable to the people relying on it. Tests and evaluations helped catch tool-call and approval regressions.

03 / Independent project

Explore the repository (opens in a new tab)

log-plat

Built for the moment
something breaks.

A distributed log pipeline in Go, built around a simple question: does every log line still arrive when a service or network connection fails?

Disk-backed batches, retries, and idempotent writes protect delivery from the agent to OpenSearch.

03A / Follow a log lineSelect a stage to explore
01 / Agent

Each batch is written to a disk spool before it is sent. The agent holds on to it until the collector confirms that Kafka has accepted it.

17↗

Fault scenarios tested.
Zero log lines lost in those runs.

02 / A little about me

One milestone.
Then, what’s next?

Curiosity got me into computer science. Seeing how far I can take a project keeps me here.

I like ambitious projects that keep growing. Every milestone makes me wonder what I could add, improve, or understand more deeply. That’s why I’m drawn to work that connects the whole system, from a useful interface to the infrastructure underneath.

At IBM and Workday, I learned that building good software also means asking better questions, sharing context, and communicating clearly with a team.
